newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq still negotiating wheat purchase -traders.
newsitem.headline: Iraq still negotiating wheat purchase -traders.

text.p: Iraq is still negotiating the purchase of French and U.S. soft wheat under a United-Nations-monitored oil-for-food deal, European grain exporters said on Tuesday.
The dealine for submitting the bids was August 15 with an answer due by August 20.
"The offers have been placed but there is no news yet. We are hoping to hear something possibly later today," one exporter close to the negotiations said.
Iraq is seeking about 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for shipment in September and October and 70,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for shipment from October onward.
French grain exporters said they were hoping Iraq would buy at least 100,000 tonnes of French wheat.
"They have the will to buy French wheat, they could buy at least 100,000 tonnes," one exporter said.
There was also talk Iraq was discussing wheat imports from Canada and Australia but details over tonnages involved were lacking.
"That may be the case but this will be hard to track down as they usually deal directly with the wheat boards," one exporter said.

The oil-for-food deal, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, took effect last December and was renewed for another six months on June 8. Iraq resumed oil exports for the second phase on August 13, having delayed these while modifying plans for aid distribution.
